title: How to edit these notes
text: 你平时主要需要编辑扩展名为 .qmd 的文件。它和 Markdown 几乎一样，但对数学公式、目录和提示框支持得更好。

title: How to edit these notes
text:
修改一篇笔记
在 VS Code 左侧文件列表中打开对应的 .qmd 文件，直接修改文字并保存即可：
## A new section

普通文字写在这里，行内公式写成 $X \to Y$。

$$
\Omega_{X/Y}=0
$$
以 --- 包围的文件开头是页面信息。通常只需要修改其中的 title 和 subtitle。

title: How to edit these notes
text:
删除一篇笔记

删除对应的 .qmd 文件。
打开项目根目录的 _quarto.yml。
在 sidebar 的 contents 中删掉指向该文件的两行，例如：

- href: "etale morphism/definitions-and-intuitions.qmd"
  text: Definitions and Intuitions
如果只删除文件而不修改 _quarto.yml，网站构建时会提示找不到页面。

title: How to edit these notes
text:
新增一篇笔记
最简单的方法是复制一篇现有的 .qmd 文件，改名并修改内容，然后在 _quarto.yml 的对应章节加入：
- href: "etale morphism/examples.qmd"
  text: Examples
以后添加新的大主题时，可以新建一个文件夹，再在 _quarto.yml 中增加一个 section。文件夹名称最好使用小写英文和连字符，例如 perfectoid-spaces。






Tip最省事的工作方式



你也可以只负责写内容，然后告诉我“把这篇笔记放到某个章节并发布”。目录、链接、渲染和推送都可以交给我处理。

title: How to edit these notes
text:
本地预览
在英文路径的工作目录 C:\notes\p-adic-geometry-note 中打开 VS Code，然后在终端运行：
.\preview-local.ps1
终端会显示一个 http://localhost:... 地址。保持这个终端运行，保存 .qmd 文件后网页会自动刷新；结束预览时按 Ctrl+C。

title: Étale Morphisms
text:
NoteSite



``An etale morphism is the analogue in algebraic geometry of a local isomorphism of manifolds in differential geometry, a covering of Riemann surfaces with no branch points in complex analysis, and an unramiﬁed extension in algebraic number theory.’’–Milne.


Since the author, I, hasn’t learned flat morphisms and unramified morphisms seriously yet, but already has a basic understanding of the étale site and étale cohomology, which means that the author is familiar to some basic properties of étale morphisms and use it. Our main goal in this chapter is to understand the various equivalent definitions of étale morphisms and to get some intuition for what they are analog to. One of the purpose of this chapter is to figure out which property of étale morphisms comes from the flatness and which property comes from the unramifiedness. The author will try to understand the definition of étale morphisms in a more intuitive way, and then try to understand the properties of étale morphisms from the perspective of flatness and unramifiedness.
For a first pass, continue to Definitions and Intuitions.
For a more detailed discussion, see Smooth Morphisms and Unramified Morphisms …(TBA)

title: Definitions
text:
NoteNote



We will list some important equivalent definitions of étale morphisms and leave the discussion of their equivalence for later.

title: Definitions
text:
Definition
A morphism \(f\colon X\to Y\) between schemes is étale if it is

locally of finite presentation,
flat, and
unramified.

title: Definitions
text:
Definition (equivalent)
A morphism \(f\colon X\to Y\) between varieties over \(k\) is étale if it induces isomorphisms on the tangent spaces at all points of \(X\).

title: Definitions
text:
Definition (equivalent)
A morphism \(f\colon X\to Y\) between schemes is étale if it is smooth of relative dimension \(0\).






TipIntuition



The second definition tells us that we can think of an étale map as a map that is locally an isomorphism. And for the definitions of the flat, unramified and smooth morphisms, see later.

title: Definitions
text:
Example: an open immersion
Every open immersion \(U\hookrightarrow X\) is étale. Nothing changes near a point of \(U\): we have only restricted our attention to a smaller open subset.

title: Definitions
text:
Example: the power map
Assume that \(n\) is invertible in the base field. On the punctured affine line, the map
\[
\mathbb G_m \longrightarrow \mathbb G_m, \qquad t\longmapsto t^n
\]
is étale. Infinitesimally, its derivative is \(nt^{n-1}\), which never vanishes on \(\mathbb G_m\).






WarningWhere the picture breaks



On the whole affine line, \(t\mapsto t^n\) ramifies at \(t=0\). The map is no longer étale there: the branches collide.

title: Unramified Morphisms
text: To study unramified morphisms, we need to understand the sheaf of differentials.

title: Unramified Morphisms
text:
Definition
For schemes \(X\) over \(Y\), there is a sheaf of differentials \(\Omega_{X/Y}\), which is a quasicoherent sheaf on \(X\).
The sheaf \(\Omega_{X/Y}\) is globally defined as the quotient \(\mathscr I/\mathscr I^2\), where the ideal sheaf \(\mathscr I\) is the sheaf of ideals defining the diagonal embedding \(X\to X\times_Y X\). One can check that \(\Omega_{X/Y}\) is indeed a sheaf on \(X\). We define a map \(d\colon \mathscr O_X\to \Omega_{X/Y}\) by \(d(f)=\operatorname{pr}_1^*f-\operatorname{pr}_2^*f\) for \(f\in \mathscr O_X\).
Affine locally, if \(X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\) and \(Y=\operatorname{Spec}(B)\), then \(\Omega_{X/Y}\) is the sheaf associated to the \(A\)-module \(\Omega_{A/B}\), which is generated by symbols \(da\) for \(a\in A\) subject to the relations: 1. \(d(a+a')=da+da'\) for all \(a,a'\in A\), 2. \(d(aa')=a\,da'+a'\,da\) for all \(a,a'\in A\), and 3. \(db=0\) for all \(b\in B\).
It is not so obvious, but one can reference to any standard textbook on algebraic geometry to see this and also the universal property of \(\Omega_{A/B}\). The module \(\Omega_{A/B}\) is universal for \(B\)-derivations from \(A\) to an \(A\)-module \(M\).

title: Unramified Morphisms
text:
Definition
A morphism \(f\colon X\to Y\) between schemes is unramified if it is locally of finite type and \(\Omega_{X/Y}=0\).
By the transitivity sequence, unramified morphisms are stable under composition. By the base change property, unramified morphisms are stable under base change. One checks that unramified morphisms are also local on the target, so they are ``reasonable’’ in the sense of the textbook the rising sea.

title: Unramified Morphisms
text:
Examples
TBA
An unramified morphism has discrete infinitesimal fibers: points upstairs do not carry tangent directions relative to the base.






ImportantInfinitesimal test



For a morphism locally of finite type, the condition \(\Omega_{X/Y}=0\) is the algebraic signal that no relative first-order motion is present.

title: Unramified Morphisms
text:
A basic example
If \(L/K\) is a finite separable field extension, then
\[
\operatorname{Spec}(L) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Spec}(K)
\]
is unramified. Separability is exactly what prevents infinitesimal ramification in this example.






WarningDo not confuse the conditions



Unramified does not by itself imply flat. Étaleness combines the unramified condition with flatness and finite presentation.

title: Unramified Morphisms
text:
A geometric criterion
Another useful slogan is that \(f\colon X\to Y\) is unramified when its diagonal \(X\to X\times_Y X\) behaves like an open immersion.

title: Smooth Morphisms
text: A smooth morphism is the relative version of a nonsingular variety. Roughly, its fibers are smooth and fit together uniformly over the base.

title: Smooth Morphisms
text:
A model example
The projection
\[
\operatorname{Spec}(R[x_1,\cdot, \cdot, x_{n+r}]/(f_1,\cdot, f_r)) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Spec}(R)
\]
is called the standard smooth morphism of relative dimension \(n\) if the determinant of the matrix
\[
\left(\frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j}\right)_{1\leq i,j\leq r}
\]
is invertible in the ring \(R[x_1,\cdot, \cdot, x_{n+r}]/(f_1,\cdot, f_r)\).






NoteRemark



The fibers of this morphism are smooth varieties of dimension \(n\) by the Jacobian criterion. The condition on the determinant is a relative version of the Jacobian criterion.

title: Smooth Morphisms
text:
Definition
A morphism \(f\colon X\to Y\) between schemes is smooth of relative dimension \(n\) if there exist open coverings \(\{U_i\}\) of \(X\) and \(\{V_i\}\) of \(Y\) such that \(f(U_i)\subseteq V_i\) and for each \(i\), the restriction \(f|_{U_i}\colon U_i\to V_i\) is a standard smooth morphism of relative dimension \(n\).

title: \(p\)-adic geometry notes
text:
My purpose is to write some informal, intuition-first notes on topics related to \(p\)-adic geometry.
Even so, there may be some proofs of results that interest me.
The aim is not to replace a textbook, but to record my study experiences in \(p\)-adic geometry.
